name: Geometry Shader Triangle Slicing (Z-Pass)
definition: A voxelization method where each triangle is clipped against the current volume slice boundaries within a geometry shader, generating triangle strips that are rasterized into the appropriate volume layer.
summary: Geometry Shader Triangle Slicing is a single-pass GPU method that clips triangles against volume slices in the geometry shader to emit precise strips, avoiding the overhead of generating and discarding unnecessary fragments in the pixel shader.
